title: Kilbirnie: the minister's origins
standfirst: Rev. John Glasgow's education and long ministry are documented. His parents, and his relationship to a contemporary Kilwinning John, remain questions for contemporary records.
question: Was Rev. John the Kilwinning John married to Barbara Allison, and were the Georges of Bog and Bay part of his family or separate local households?
answer: University and Fasti entries document the minister's career but name no parents. The Kilwinning John and Barbara Alason household is a serious duplicate candidate, while the retrospective Bog and Bay Georges lack dates and stated relationships. A wider Corsankell–Stevenston–Kilwinning route is a hypothesis, not a pedigree.

chapters.period: 1676–1699 · two uncertain fathers and one mother
chapters.title: Kilwinning and Irvine: the remaining early family heads
body: Select John Glasgow-3375 as the uncertain working father of James Glasgow-3105. James is the combined working father account behind the two 1689 Kilwinning child entries, one naming Margaret Park. John is a record-defined father in that same parish in 1679 and 1689, associated with Barbara Alason/Allason. The rough 1650 and 1670 family generations would put John at about twenty when James was born, and both generations could have children recorded during 1689. Neither year is a recorded birth; John’s captured before-about 1661 boundary is an adult-status estimate and permits an earlier birth. No date is changed to fit this placement. Prefer this recorded local adult as a provisional parent-generation anchor over assigning James directly to the older John-1604 scaffold or to an otherwise unidentified father. The shared parish and compatible generational spacing supply the logic, at very low confidence; no source names James as John’s son.

John-1604 remains a possible older father rather than a rejected alternative. His approximate 1626 birth and 1664 death are unsourced; a literal 1670 James birth would conflict with that death estimate, requiring at least one estimate to be wrong. Neither is silently adjusted. Hew-1066 or another local Glasgow remains possible; the current shortlist is not exhaustive. John-3375 may be the same man as the minister John-1073. If so, the minister’s approximate 1653 generation would imply younger parenthood around 1670, still dependent on James’s unrecorded birth. No merge, proved brotherhood, ministerial occupation for John-3375 or new father for the minister is inferred. John’s own attachment to John-1604 and the older Hugh-1603 scaffold retain their existing uncertainty. Barbara Alason is the recorded/probable mother of John’s known children, not a newly selected mother of James. James’s mother stays unknown. Margaret Park is recorded for the July 1689 child; Anne’s May 1689 index omits a mother. The combined James father account and the two children’s sibling status remain provisional. Two index/baptism dates two months apart do not prove two births to one mother. No witness, occupation, property or inheritance bridge ties James to John.

Select Hew Glasgow-1066 and Margaret Lachland-2 as the uncertain working father and mother of Hugh Glasgow-3109, the Irvine father with Jean Service in 1696, through the existing strong possible identity with their 1676 Kilwinning child Hew Glasgow-1067. If baptised near birth, the child would have been about twenty in 1696. The name variant Hew/Hugh, compatible generation and neighbouring Ayrshire parish setting make this a practical preferred childhood comparison. This activates a comparison already explicitly retained in both profiles, rather than treating the 1696 child’s entry as the adult father’s birth. Maternity is assessed independently from the 1676 child clause: the supplied Scotland’s People index explicitly names Margaret Lachland with Hew Glasgow. The Findmypast transcript abbreviates/queries her name as Mt Lach?. Margaret is not selected merely because she is Hew’s spouse. Both adult parent links depend on the uncertain childhood identity and remain uncertain; the child’s recorded parentage is not proof of the adult’s origins.

Keep Glasgow-1067 and Glasgow-3109 as separate profile accounts of a possible single man. The shared parents do not establish two distinct sons called Hew/Hugh. No record joins the 1676 child to the 1696 Irvine father or proves the proposed sequence from Jean Service to Mary Dean from 1699; no death, remarriage or continuous personal identifier has been supplied. The Mary Dean family retains its own unproved childhood-to-adult identification. The older Hew-1066 himself is a possible alternative identity of the 1696 father, rather than simultaneously being his proved father. That alternative would invalidate the selected child identity and the maternal transfer; it is not materialised alongside them. A different unrecorded Hugh remains possible. The 1677 preacher has no inspected residence or kin bridge here; the selected 1676 child could not have been that adult preacher a year later. The 1751 Irvine/London sailor remains an unselected occupational identity, not an event newly assigned to either account. Retain the literal source discrepancies: the official supplied index and Findmypast give24 May 1676, while the older father biography reports5 May from FamilySearch. A24 May marriage is also reported in that family biography; the original page and event type were not re-read. No baptism, birthday or ceremony date is newly corrected or proved. Hugh-3109’s before-about 1676 boundary remains an estimate, not a birth record or a hard exclusion of the 1676 child. Existing Jean Service co-parentage, both 1696 children, Mary Dean associations and the child’s parent-field grades are retained. No relationship-certainty change is counted. Margaret is not assigned to any other child whose record does not name her.

These are selected uncertain working relationships using existing material, not new original-record discoveries. No vital date, location, existing spouse or attached relative is cleared, and no identity merge, live WikiTree save or confidence upgrade is claimed. Counts concern retained profile accounts and inherit uncertainty and possible duplicates in older links.

chapters.title: Select the local father while keeping the alternatives
body: Select Glasgow-1604 as the uncertain working father of Rev. Glasgow-1073. The minister’s approximate 1653 birth fits an approximate 1626 father generation, and his Kilbirnie ministry and Robertland-Cunningham marriage belong to the Ayrshire setting of the Kilwinning profile. This adopts the leading existing-profile comparison already recorded in the research. Glasgow-1604’s attached adult sons have Kilwinning and Ayr households, making this a more economical local family placement than importing the minister into Glasgow-1078’s Glasgow-city household. No inspected record names the minister’s father; the preference rests on generation and locality, with low confidence.

Glasgow-1604 is a tree-derived generation: his c.1626 birth, c.1664 death and parentage are unproved. The minister’s c.1653 birth is inferred from his reported age at death, not a baptism. Glasgow-3375, father with Barbara Alason in Kilwinning in 1679 and January 1689, remains a possible duplicate of the minister before his recorded January 1690 marriage. The two profile accounts are retained separately; their shared proposed father does not establish two distinct sons or brotherhood. No merge is selected. The former Glasgow-1078 father remains an uncertain, unselected alternative. The captured Cunningham-22604 mother is independently unproved; her tree attachment to Robert does not establish the minister’s maternity or make her Glasgow-1604’s wife. No new mother or spouse is assigned. The working route above Glasgow-1604 through Hugh Glasgow-1603 and James Glasgow-991 remains an unsupported older scaffold. The suggested Corsankell route is another unresolved ancestry comparison; this selection does not establish either path to the sixteenth-century family. The minister’s child-group audit remains open. Profile-based connectivity counts do not resolve duplicates or turn any uncertain link into documented descent. No new original inspection, confidence upgrade or live WikiTree edit is claimed.

chapters.title: A documented ministry
body: John graduated M.A. at Glasgow in 1674 and was ordained at Kilbirnie in 1688; Fasti records his death in 1721.
His marriage to Jean Cunningham and later family evidence describe a life and ministry, but do not name a father or mother.

evidence.label: Rev. John: career, ancestry and identity problem

chapters.title: A contemporary Kilwinning John
body: OPR index citations associate John Glasgow and Barbara Alason with local events in 1679 and 1689.
Those entries define a contemporary household but need their original pages before they can distinguish or merge the man with the minister.

evidence.label: Kilwinning John: household and duplicate assessment

chapters.title: Bog, Bay and the older route
body: A FamilySearch-catalogued handwritten genealogy mentions Georges of the Bog and Bay while asking about the minister's connection.
The note does not establish dates, parentage or identity, so it cannot attach either George to the minister or identify the Bay bearer with an existing profile.
